reviews.author: Damon Horn
reviews.text:
The location is absolutely beautiful and the architecture is breathtaking. The trails are a very pleasant and the site was clearly set up with care. The exhibits are engaging and use technology well. I only have 2 complaints:

1) It took around 30-40 minutes to get in. The line was moving very slowly because the digital check in kiosks took a while.

2) I asked the AI Teddy Roosevelt a question ("Did you support Eugene Debs imprisonment for protesting the draft?") The computer had to think for a long time, then basically said that while he disagreed with Debs, freedom of speech is important and he should have the right to say what he wants. I researched the exact question later and found that TR had said many negative things specifically about Debs and had written in support of jailing people for opposing WWI and the draft. It was disappointing to have received inaccurate information in the library, and a reminder that AI can be tricky and overconfident. I wish the AI exhibit had simply said it didn't know the answer instead of making something up that didn't fit the facts.

Alternatively you could have a docent or TR impersonator answer questions, which I have seen work well at other museums.

Despite these two quibbles, the museum is overall excellent and I enjoyed myself.

reviews.text: Hit up several presidential libraries on my travels--Lincoln, Reagan, Nixon--and never once needed a timed ticket. Just showed up and went in. Then I drove way out to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in the middle of North Dakota, and they turned me away at the door because I didn't have a reservation. Twenty-six bucks to get in and not even close to busy. No flexibility, no accommodation, just a flat no. You're not the Louvre out there, folks. A little hospitality wouldn't hurt.

reviews.author: Benjamin
reviews.title: If You’re Looking for North Dakota Hospitality, This Ain’t It.
reviews.text: I’ve visited several presidential libraries across the country, including Lincoln in Springfield, Reagan in Simi Valley, and Nixon in Yorba Linda. None of them required timed tickets—you could simply walk in. So I drove hours out of my way to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota, only to be turned away at the door because I didn’t have a reservation. I explained the long drive and asked if there was any way to accommodate us, but the staff member seemed almost offended by the request and offered no sympathy or flexibility whatsoever. At twenty-six dollars a ticket and with the place clearly not crowded, that kind of attitude feels completely out of place for a destination this remote.

Once you make it through the first exhibit, there is adequate seating options to rest at before venturing to other exhibits. Try to bring as little as possible so your hands won’t be tied up and you can easily access the interactive exhibits. There are clean restrooms available upon walking in and within the main area. Food is available on site too. Plan in your budget to find something at the gift shop! A lot of great options to find a keepsake of your experience.

reviews.title: Wonderful trip to Theodore Roosevelt library
reviews.text:
The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota, is one of the state's premier attractions and sits on a bluff overlooking Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

The exhibits tell Theodore Roosevelt's life story, from a rancher in the Badlands to the 26th U.S. president.

Interactive galleries, artifacts, and multimedia experiences.
Stunning architecture designed to blend into the Badlands landscape.

Scenic walking trails and overlooks with panoramic views.

reviews.title: Educational experience but they’re still working on some issues.
reviews.text: The library is beautiful. The problem is getting to the library because the signage is so poorly done. Our friend requires a handicap parking space for which there was absolutely zero signs to indicate how to get there. We asked one of the employees where those parking spaces were and she said that the pavement is marked, but when people parked over them, no one else even realizes that they are there. Once you park, it is still quite a hike to get up to the entrance to the library. I only saw one or two shuttles that were available to take people who needed additional assistance to get from the limited parking area up to the entrance. After you get to the entrance you get in a line and wait to be sent through a freestanding scanner. The scanner later blew over & broke when a wind storm blew through. Once you’re cleared to go in, there’s another line to get in to go through to get your ticket scanned. Then you’re given the opportunity to sign up with your wristband to be able to take pictures of yourself throughout the library. If you decide to go, I recommend planning a full day in order to stop and read every single display that they have. It’s very interesting & educational but it’s also very time-consuming and daunting, especially if there’s large crowds. The observation of the four of us in our group decided that we much more enjoyed the Bush library we have been through in Texas.
reviews.response_text:
Thank you for a detailed and useful review. On the accessible parking, you're right and it's a design failure rather than bad luck - markings painted on the pavement are no use once a vehicle is on top of them. Better signage is a priority fix.

On the shuttles: those golf carts run from the drop-off circle for anyone who needs them, and your friend shouldn't have had to make that walk. The fact you saw only one or two and read it as scarcity tells us we aren't making the service visible enough, which is on us. Ask any Welcome team member, or call ahead on 701-892-6070. More at trlibrary.com/visit/accessibility

Thank you also for flagging the scanner. That has gone to the operations team.

- The team at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

You're the second visitor to flag the Rough Riders video specifically. It's being looked at.

On the objects: some of what's on display are reproductions, and where that's the case the labels should say so plainly. If you came across ones that didn't, tell us which and we'll check them — that's a fair thing to expect and an easy thing to fix.  The Library has many original objects including his diary, Rough Rider uniform, buckskin outfit, objects from the Smithsonian–Roosevelt African expedition, his hunting rifles, the Lincoln portrait from his office in with White House and diplomatic gifts from his time as President, and the eyeglass case, and shirt from the assassination attempt among many others.   We hope you will come back we are looking into digital curator tours that can help guide people through the history of the original objects on display.

— The team at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

reviews.text:
This is a well constructed museum experience, though I don't know enough to know if it constitutes a "Presidential Library". Some of the experiences and moments of Theodore Roosevelt's life are very well orchestrated, such as the presentation of his tragic loss and the diary entry after. Some of the experiences felt less than they could have been with the computer generated/AI elements. I did not interact with the AI Teddy because it feels hollow and not worth the time, with all the other moments being more impactful.

There is some sad irony in the trust-busting and monopoly-fighting that TR did alongside the nature of how this place came together, as well as the current push to take, end, or sell public lands to the highest bidders which Teddy probably would be turning in his grave over.

The (literal) windows to the Badlands sprinkled throughout  the walking experience were well architected and planned.  The walk along the roof and the building melding into the Badlands is well done.

reviews.author: Obaidullah Rahim
reviews.text:
The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library exceeded every expectation. This is far more than a library - it’s an unforgettable experience that perfectly blends history, architecture, technology, and the breathtaking beauty of the North Dakota Badlands. Every exhibit is immersive, thoughtfully designed, and engaging for visitors of all ages. You don’t just learn about Theodore Roosevelt’s life - you feel connected to his journey and the values that shaped him.

The building itself is a masterpiece, seamlessly blending into the surrounding landscape, and the panoramic views alone are worth the visit. The interactive exhibits kept us engaged for hours, and the staff was welcoming, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about sharing Roosevelt’s legacy.

If you’re anywhere near Medora or Theodore Roosevelt National Park, this is an absolute must-see. I came away inspired, educated, and with an even greater appreciation for conservation, leadership, and American history. Without a doubt, one of the best museums and historical attractions I’ve ever visited.

reviews.text:
Amazing place!!! My very active 11,9&6 year old boys really liked it and never were bored (just hungry at the end) for 2.5 hours. Walk the roof and the grounds in the morning before the summer noon temperatures. Inside, the kids can find hidden animals in about seven of the rooms while the adults read all the materials in the room (and the adults can look for the animals too). In the middle is the White House gang, which is very fun information but is actually a play area for kids with rubber building blocks and rope bridges. A little ways before that there is digital cow hearding and an electric shooting game that four people can play -- this is in the area you learn about TR as a cowboy. Follow the map of the museum and use your wrist band at the progress check kiosks to make sure you haven't missed anything. You also get to see yourself in seven different scenes, make an election poster and campaign for yourself, and a fee other activities-- ALL of which are emailed to the email you provided at check in when you get your wristband and take your photo before the tour.
So much to see, my wife and I will definitely be back to see what all we missed.

reviews.text: I have visited many museums, including presidential museums all over the country, and this one is the most amazing museum I have ever visited! The details integrated with technology made it interactive, educational, and fun.  Adults and kids will love putting themselves into history while they learn about the life and times of Theodore Roosevelt. The construction of the museum was also well done. The design of the walls mimicking the layers of soil in the surrounding area to the large windows showing the exterior landscape showcases the thoughtful design. The building feels like it belongs in the landscape. It is 100% worth the drive to see. My kids are already asking when we can return!

We had parked our car, and went through security, then come to find out that you need to buy tickets to visit a library. I had no idea, no libraries near us do that. I asked, how much it was, and one of the security girls had to ask the other one, who said it was $26 (check online if you want to confirm). I figured since we already drove up here,  I would buy them,  so I told her that I would be purchasing them for my family, and she said that they already had sold out yesterday. So that was a letdown. 

The outdoor of the library was beautiful. You could tell that everything looks brand new. There were people singing near the rocking chairs, although they were singing pretty explicit things with families around. I'm not sure how it is with those people, but had my parents been with me, like theirs were with them, it would make me really uncomfortable to be with my parents and hear those songs. 
I would have given them five stars even if I wasn't able to go into the library if workers do not have to ask each other how much the price of the tickets are, and those explicit songs. On the plus side, the bathrooms were clean.  They also had a water bottle refill fountain right by the bathrooms.
reviews.response_text:
We're sorry - parking, clearing security and then finding out you couldn't get in is a bad sequence, and the ticketing should have been obvious long before that point. We're working on making it clearer well before anyone leaves home.  Summer is a busy season for Medora and anyone looking to visit from June-September we highly recommend booking in advance online.

The singing near the rocking chairs shouldn't have happened with families around, and thank you for telling us. That's gone to the grounds team.

You also shouldn't have had to wait while two staff worked out the admission price. That's a training gap and a fair thing to be annoyed about.

Thank you for the note about the restrooms and the water refill station. Small things, easy to get wrong.

- The team at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

reviews.author: Stewart King
reviews.text: An amazing museum with a comprehensive portrait of the man and his times. They did a good job of presenting the complexity and historical context. The exhibits were interesting, though they didn't actually have a lot of Roosevelt items; most of the documents and items they present are replicas of items that you can see in the original at Oyster Bay or (for the documents) at Harvard. I didn't do the interactive features but young people who were using them seemed to be amused; if I was there with kids I would certainly have participated. The architecture and grounds are fantastic! You get a good sense of the place and what it must have felt like to live here more than a century ago. What this is not is a library - Roosevelt's papers are at Harvard and even the tchotchke shop was very light on books. I was actually looking for Darren Lunde's The Naturalist, on Roosevelt's environmental initiatives, and didn't find it. The 25 bucks to get in was somewhat of a surprise but this is a private foundation, not the Park Service or the Archives, so be warned. Nevertheless, I recommend a visit to flesh out your experience in the stunning National Park next door.

They claim that your info and image is deleted after 30 days, but not sure I believe that.

Minus 1 star due to how terrible gift shop is, Hardly anything there for souvenirs with the actual “Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library” on it. No magnets, no stickers, slim selection of shirts; very sad we didn’t get our usual tourist magnet and/or sticker for our collections.

Otherwise, the library/museum is informative and showcases his life well, just wish it didn’t rely so heavily on AI. Very surprising that everything isn’t protected from people touching them.
reviews.response_text:
E,

Thank you for visiting.  The Trailblazer and AI photo stations are not required for participants.  While we encourage it you can still enjoy the original TR objects, films, and traditional museum displays.  Most interactives still offer an ability to tap and participate without regsitering.

We do delete the information after 30 days, that is important for anyone who wants to keep their photos and videos generated.  We are not preserving those long-term.

There are additional items available in our online shop that have TRPL branded logos.  We are still scaling up our shops inventory and sold out. of many items during the opening week.

Thank you for your feedback and we hope you had a safe journey.

reviews.text:
Mixed feelings about it.  I learned a few things. I noticed some of the object labels had text that sounded rather 'woke', not necessarily a quote from TR but rather someone's thoughts on what he said.  A lot of messaging about 'how you should be'.

This is not a museum with 1000's and 1000's of artifacts. Some good tech but generally speaking this place did not exude warmth - instead it was bright, with a lot of tech which came off as cold and many times shallow. It seems out of balance at many points, providing space & over-the-top presentation for something that would be better served up in a simple, direct way. Did I learn more about him, yes. Do I feel more connected to TR, taking pride in him as a man - no. So the info was there but the meaning wasn't.

No printed receipt. You have to provide your email address if you want a receipt. A place this large, with so many attendees does not provide a printed receipt. You can provide your email, plus you can get your photo taken of your face so the AI programs can photoshop you into a different outfit. reviews.response_text:

This is the first presidential library that I have visited, and it has set the bar incredibly high for an future presidential library visits!

This library is visually stunning, thoughtfully arranged, and extremely interactive and informative.  I was a little worried about how well our kids (ages 7, 11, and 14) would do at something like this, but we spent between 4-5 hours there without a single complaint.

I'd recommend buying tickets ahead of time to reserve a spot and save a few minutes on your way in.  When you arrive, there is free parking and then you head to the breezeway between the two buildings (library on one side and event and office space on the other).  You'll go through a security point before you enter and they do not allow any guns or knives of any sort in the building so I'd leave them in your car if you have them.

Once you enter you will get a bracelet to wear that has a chip in it that will give you access to all of the interactive parts of the library.  Then you'll register your bracelet with your name, email, and photo and head into the exhibits.  (The photo is for some some of the AI generated images. See pics below. But if you're worried big brother is watching, you can probably skip it if you want, but I'd highly recommend it.  Our kids thought it was awesome and hilarious.) You will get an email with your photos and also other parts of the experience that are a part of your "journal".

The exhibits walk through different phases of TR's life and experiences and lets you join in the experience in almost every area of the library.

TR and his family loved animals, so throughout the museum exhibits are animals you can try and find and scan with your bracelet to collect them all.  Our younger two had fun trying to find them all and it got them excited to travel from room to room.  Our 14 year old enjoyed the different interactive pieces of different exhibits too.

You can also do some walks outside and on the roof of the building!  Very fun and unique experience with incredible views.

If you're in the area, I can't recommend this place enough for you (and your family)! We did the library from 9-1:30, TR National Park from 2-5 (ate picnic lunch in the car), dinner from 5:30-6:30, and the Medora Musical to cap our day.  Great family trip! Hope you have as much fun as we did!

Not only that, it comes across as very cheap.  TR would never support this. I am disappointed to say the least.
Besides the AI, I think the TR Presidential Library is actually pretty great. Very structurally beautiful, with creative and visually engaging exhibits for people of all ages. Somewhat disappointed by my experience. Heavy use of AI and an over-reliance on interactive features for kids. At times, it felt more like a Disney World attraction made to entertain, as opposed to an educational experience.

Ok, first, the positives:  the narrative of Theodore’s presidency was pretty well-balanced, and some of the video exhibits (especially the narrations) were excellent. The facility itself and the surrounding landscape are absolutely stunning and are reason enough to visit the library.

The negatives: the pacing of the museum isn’t always coherent, as highly important moments of Theodore’s life, political rise, and presidency are condensed down to a sentence or two on signage.  The AI component is also jarring. In one exhibit featuring an AI enhanced image of Theodore and the Rough Riders, one of the soldiers’ faces appears twice in the image. This is especially odd given that the actual image is rather well-known and could’ve been displayed without alteration.

I was excited to go, and believe that the place has great potential, but I don’t think I’d recommend it at this point. Hopefully they figure out a way to incorporate the AI in a way that is less obnoxious!

reviews.text:
Tl;dr: For the sake of fairness, I will try to ignore my tremendous bias, as I am an ardent admirer of Theodore Roosevelt (henceforth referred to as TR). That being said, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is an experience unparalleled. “It was here that the romance of my life began” - TR

Service and Price: Memberships at the library cover admission, and regular tickets can be had at different price points for military, students, seniors, and children. All the staff, from the cafe to the janitors to the curators, were second to none! Friendly, passionate, and professional from start to finish.

Experience: Depending on how fast you want to go and how many things you want to do, it will take 2-4 hours to get through the whole exhibit. The first thing you are prompted to do is take a photo at one of their photo stations. Part of the museum experience is interactive, and they take your photo and show you what you would look like if you were part of TR’s entourage throughout significant events of his life, which is tracked via a bracelet given to you at the beginning of the self guided tour. The museum takes you through the life of TR, starting as a child. You journey through his childhood home, his time in the Badlands, his return to politics, his career in government service, and what he did after his career. Each portion of his life is prefaced in the main hall, off which the immersive exhibits all branch. There are numerous items from his life that are on display, and it is all expertly curated. Of course, they do have everything to keep adults engaged, but they also have a good number of activities to keep the kids engaged as well. I would jump at the opportunity to go again, and fully intend to return upon my next journey to Medora.

Location: The TR Presidential Library is located in the North Dakota Badlands, in the town of Medora. It is up a very steep hill, so walking to it would be very difficult, but they share a parking lot with the Medora Musical, so once you get up the hill, parking is plentiful and the walk into and around the building is flat and easy. And for those wondering, Theodore Roosevelt spent a few years ranching around Medora, after his mother and wife passed away on the same day, the latter of whom had just given birth to this daughter. He chose to come to Medora because he appreciated the desolate and haunting beauty of the land, but also the simplicity and honest nature of the work and lifestyle. By his own admission, his experiences here were what helped shape him into the incredible leader he became.

Grounds and Interior: The first thing you see as you crest the hill is how the museum rises gracefully from the earth, while still being part of it like a natural hill. Native plants decorate the rooftop, which you can walk onto via a meandering walking path on one side, and staircase on the other. Another walking path about half a mile long takes you on a large flat loop in front of the museum to showcase some of the quiet beauty the badlands offer.  All parts of the grounds are wheelchair accessible. To enter the museum, you walk through a massive breezeway, which offers rocking chairs and a view overlooking the town below. The whole building extensively includes natural materials throughout, including wood flooring and rammed earth walls. The massive windows really open up the space, and bring the outdoors into your experience.

Overall: As a true Theodore Roosevelt fan, this is as pure of an experience as you can have. You get to experience all of the highs and lows and adventures of TR’s life. It does an excellent job at not only showing you what his life was like, but immersing you into each part of his journey. The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is an absolute must see, even if you are only driving through. Your time will be well rewarded with incredible history at a world class facility.
